newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Sasol in fuel-from-gas talks with Qatar.
newsitem.headline: Sasol in fuel-from-gas talks with Qatar.

text.p: South African synthetic fuel producer Sasol Ltd said on Wednesday it was holding discussions with the Qatar General Petroleum Corp with the intention of establishing a project to convert natural gas to liquid fuels.

The proposed project would be sited at Ras Laffan in Qatar and would convert some of Qatar's abundant natural gas reserves into transportation liquid fuels, such as diesel, using Sasol's commercially-proven technology, Sasol said in a statement.
The two parties are currently holding talks about forming a joint venture.
The infrastructure that has been put into place at Ras Laffan and the government's willingness to provide an attractive climate for gas-based projects made the project promising, it added.
"This proposed project will allow for the State of Qatar to broaden its portfolio of gas utilisation projects," Sasol said.

Initially, only two trains are expected to be installed, with a total production capacity of around 20,000 barrels a day of liquid fuels. But this could be increased by the addition of further trains at a later stage.
